analysis.overview.entrySkill: Read a simple table and explain the decision it should support.
analysis.overview.reason: Begin with the question and observation grain before a tool.

excel.overview.entrySkill: Recognize a row, column, cell and a simple arithmetic expression.
excel.overview.reason: The current local offering is a question set; use the linked foundation reading where instruction is missing.

sql.overview.entrySkill: Recognize a table, row and column.
sql.overview.reason: Introductory query practice does not require completion of Fabric or Power BI.

python.overview.entrySkill: Understand basic programming ideas: variables, conditions and iteration.
python.overview.reason: The official Python tutorial targets existing programmers; it is not evidence that a complete novice programming course exists here.

fabric.foundations.entrySkill: Distinguish a dataset, table, analytical workload and storage from processing.
fabric.foundations.reason: Fabric orientation precedes workload-specific choices; the official entry path recommends basic data terminology.

fabric.ingestion.entrySkill: Distinguish referencing, replicating and retaining data; identify source and access constraints.
fabric.ingestion.reason: Movement choices use OneLake/item boundaries. Transformation is not a universal prerequisite for learning ingestion.

fabric.transform.entrySkill: Identify table state, source data and the intended output of a transformation.
fabric.transform.reason: Transformation lessons operate on data whose storage and arrival are already understood.

fabric.query.entrySkill: Read SELECT, filtering, grouping and join intent.
fabric.query.reason: Query surfaces require relational-query concepts; a full transformation course is not mandatory.

fabric.model.entrySkill: Explain fact/dimension grain, relationships and a measure.
fabric.model.reason: Semantic-model decisions build on dimensional concepts, not just platform vocabulary.

fabric.security.entrySkill: Identify the principal, object, access path and least-privilege requirement.
fabric.security.reason: Security concepts are needed before production access; they are not postponed until after advanced streaming.

fabric.delivery.entrySkill: Understand workspace boundaries, permissions and the item being promoted or monitored.
fabric.delivery.reason: Operational deployment integrates platform and access concepts. This preparation does not claim every item supports every deployment feature.

fabric.streaming.entrySkill: Distinguish events, streams, ingestion and an analytical query.
fabric.streaming.reason: The official RTI introductory module expects Fabric core concepts, not prior completion of all SQL, DAX or deployment lessons.

fabric.overview.entrySkill: Identify the workload and constraints in a cross-topic decision.
fabric.overview.reason: Cross-topic collections are reference/transfer material, not a final mandatory prerequisite node.

statistics.foundations.entrySkill: Read a table and basic arithmetic.
statistics.foundations.reason: Population, sample, variable and parameter are the entry vocabulary of the source.

statistics.describe.entrySkill: Identify the observational unit and variable type.
statistics.describe.reason: Center and spread describe data before inference is attempted.

statistics.probability.entrySkill: Interpret proportions and distinguish an event from an observation.
statistics.probability.reason: Probability supplies the language for distributions and uncertainty.

statistics.distributions.entrySkill: Distinguish a discrete count from a continuous measurement; interpret center/spread.
statistics.distributions.reason: PMF, density and distribution parameters require probability and descriptive vocabulary.

statistics.sampling.entrySkill: Distinguish one sample, a population and a statistic across repeated samples.
statistics.sampling.reason: Standard error and intervals require a sampling distribution, rather than treating data spread as estimator uncertainty.

statistics.hypothesis.entrySkill: Distinguish a null model, sampling variability, statistic and standard error.
statistics.hypothesis.reason: A test statistic and p-value belong after sampling, not in elementary population/sample vocabulary.

statistics.experiments.entrySkill: Distinguish assignment, treatment, outcome and chance variation.
statistics.experiments.reason: Design and randomization can be introduced before formal testing; inferential interpretation additionally uses the hypothesis topic.

statistics.relationships.entrySkill: Read a paired observation and distinguish association from a causal claim.
statistics.relationships.reason: Describing correlation does not require completing experimental design; causal interpretation needs its safeguards.

statistics.synthesis.entrySkill: Choose a method and state assumptions, uncertainty and the decision boundary.
statistics.synthesis.reason: The integrated source case combines description, inference and interpretation. Reference sheets remain available earlier.

visualization.foundations.entrySkill: Identify the decision, observational grain and variable types.
visualization.foundations.reason: Start with the question, not a preferred chart or software tool.

visualization.comparison.entrySkill: Recognize categories, numerical values and a comparison baseline.
visualization.comparison.reason: Comparison requires suitable encodings and scale rather than advanced probability.

visualization.distribution.entrySkill: Interpret a numerical variable, center, spread and outliers.
visualization.distribution.reason: A histogram or box plot explains variation, not just a categorical ranking.

visualization.relationships.entrySkill: Read paired observations and explain association without a causal claim.

visualization.time.entrySkill: Distinguish ordered time from an arbitrary category and identify a baseline.
visualization.time.reason: Time-series reading needs time ordering and context, not completion of all distribution labs.

visualization.composition.entrySkill: Name the audience, comparison task and accessible encoding.
visualization.composition.reason: Dashboard/story synthesis integrates simpler views; the audience lesson itself may be read at the start.

visualization.accessibility.entrySkill: Distinguish color, label and non-color cues.
visualization.accessibility.reason: Accessibility and visual integrity are design constraints from the start, not an optional advanced afterthought.

visualization.overview.entrySkill: Choose a topic or a source collection.
visualization.overview.reason: Library maps, references and interview collections are not prerequisite bottlenecks.

power-bi.prepare.entrySkill: Identify data types, rows and the intended analytical output.
power-bi.prepare.reason: Preparation is an entry capability; no Fabric course completion is required.

power-bi.model.entrySkill: Explain grain, keys and the difference between a fact and dimension.
power-bi.model.reason: The star-schema guidance ties model structure to analytical meaning and preparation.

power-bi.report.entrySkill: Identify the measure and audience, and read a model relationship.
power-bi.report.reason: A report is built on model meaning and usable visual encoding.

power-bi.govern.entrySkill: Distinguish model, report, workspace, user and access boundary.
power-bi.govern.reason: Governance depends on knowing which artifact and audience is being secured or delivered.

power-bi.overview.entrySkill: Identify which Power BI capability the question is testing.
power-bi.overview.reason: Mixed-topic practice is not a separate advanced subject or a universal prerequisite.
